battle.name: 辛亥革命
battle.brief: 辛亥革命於一九一一年十月十日在武昌爆發起義，各省陸續宣布獨立或響應革命，清廷統治根基迅速動搖。英國皇家海軍於一八七七年列裝Thornycroft 27節型魚雷艇，HMS Viper為其代表，專門執行高速近海反艦與魚雷突擊任務，是英國早期海上突擊兵力。

kit.name: 魚雷艇
kit.history: 魚雷艇編入英國皇家海軍水面艦隊，定位為近海快速反艦與巡邏力，以輕型水面艦艇承擔突擊任務，隸屬沿岸防衛與艦隊支援體系。

countries: 這場戰爭不是兩個現代國家之間的全面戰爭，而是大清帝國中央軍、各省原有部隊與革命軍在清帝退位前形成的分裂性內戰。湖北、湖南、江西、山西、雲南、浙江、江蘇、廣東、四川等地的革命軍先後設立軍政府或宣布脫離清廷；上海、南京被攻克後，革命軍於一九一二年一月一日建立中華民國臨時政府。因此，交戰方應記為大清一方，以及由各省革命軍演變而成的共和一方。英國、日本等列強沒有以本國軍隊正式加入戰局，但武器供應、對外航運、金融往來與外交承認，都是清廷和革命政府必須計算的外部條件。
countriesEn: This war was not a full-scale conflict between two modern states. It was a fragmented civil war among the central government of the Qing Empire, provincial troops already under the authority of provincial governors, and revolutionary armies before the emperor abdicated. Revolutionary forces in Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Shanxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Guangdong, and Sichuan successively established military governments or declared separation from the Qing court. After Shanghai and Nanjing fell, the revolutionaries established the Provisional Government of the Republic of China on January 1, 1912. The belligerents should therefore be identified as the Qing side and the republican side that developed from the provincial revolutionary armies. Britain, Japan, and other powers did not formally enter the fighting with their own national troops, but arms supply, overseas shipping, financial flows, and diplomatic recognition were external factors that both the Qing court and the revolutionary government had to take into account.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩套軍事政治體系。革命方面，湖北新軍領袖蔡鍔在武昌起義當夜協助調動部隊，第八鎮協統黎元洪其後被推為湖北軍政府都督；黃興先於三月在廣州起義，十一月再赴漢口主持鄂軍作戰；徐達指揮進攻南京並參與籌劃北伐；陳其美掌握上海革命軍的籌劃，其後在南京受傷去世；山西由李烈鈞等主持起義，浙江由呂公望等率軍光復杭州；孫中山在海外推動組織與籌款，被推選為臨時大總統；唐紹儀則代表革命政府同袁世凱方面談判。清廷方面，湖廣總督瑞澂在武昌失守後撤離，北洋軍由馮國璋、段祺瑞等率領南下，張勳主持江南防務，兩江總督張人駿在南京陷落時身亡。袁世凱掌握北洋主力，先奉清廷之命作戰，後來成為決定停戰與政權交接的關鍵人物。
peopleEn: The principal figures belonged to two military-political systems. On the revolutionary side, Hubei New Army leader Cai E helped mobilize troops on the night of the Wuchang uprising, and the commander of the Hubei Eighth Division, Li Yuanhong, was subsequently chosen as governor of the Hubei Military Government. Huang Xing had led the March uprising in Guangzhou and arrived at Hankou in November to direct the Hubei forces. Xu Da commanded the assault on Nanjing and later helped plan the Northern Expeditions. Chen Qimei organized revolutionary activity in Shanghai and was wounded and killed after the fighting at Nanjing. Li Liejun and other officers led the Shanxi uprising, while Lü Gongwang and others led the Zhejiang forces that took Hangzhou. Sun Yat-sen coordinated revolutionary organization and fundraising from abroad and was elected provisional president. Tang Shaoyi represented the revolutionary government in negotiations with the Yuan Shikai faction. On the Qing side, Huguang viceroy Ruicheng withdrew after Wuchang fell. Beiyang troops were sent south under commanders including Feng Guozhang and Duan Qirui, while Zhang Xun directed the Jiangnan defenses. Liangjiang viceroy Zhang Renjun died when Nanjing was lost. Yuan Shikai controlled the main Beiyay force, initially fought for the Qing court, and later became the decisive figure in the armistice and transfer of political authority.
kits: 交戰所用裝備以當時已列裝的型號為限。湖北與北洋步兵大量使用7.92×57公厘 Gewehr 88 栓動步槍，漢陽兵工廠製型配五發彈匣；清廷各鎮也保有同口徑步槍與相應子彈。機槍為7.92×57公厘 Maxim 1888式水冷重機槍及漢陽仿製型，架設於專用三腳架或車座。砲兵包括克虜伯75毫米野戰砲、克虜伯57毫米速射砲，以及北洋軍列裝的120毫米克虜伯榴彈炮。十月十一日漢陽軍械與十一月三日江南製造局落入革命軍後，7.92毫米步槍彈、Maxim機槍彈、75毫米砲彈、瞄準附件與炮車零件，成為鄂軍、上海軍及南京方面的重要補給；但各部隊領用不同批次器材，備件和炮車附件不完全配套。京漢鐵路、滬寧線與長江船運決定重砲、彈藥箱和傷員運輸速度，前線也常因鐵路切換、橋梁搶修、馬匹不足而中斷補給。
kitsEn: The equipment used in the fighting was limited to types already in service at the time. Hubei and Beiyang infantry used large quantities of 7.92×57 mm Gewehr 88 bolt-action rifles, with the Hanyang Arsenal pattern fitted with five-round box magazines. Qing provincial formations also held rifles of the same caliber and matching ammunition. Machine-gun equipment consisted of the 7.92×57 mm Maxim 1888 water-cooled heavy machine gun and the Hanyang copy, mounted on purpose-built tripods or vehicle mounts. The artillery inventory included Krupp 75 mm field guns, Krupp 57 mm quick-firing guns, and the 120 mm Krupp howitzers fielded by the Beiyang forces. After the Hanyang armory and, on November 3, the Jiangnan Arsenal came under revolutionary control, Gewehr 88 ammunition, Maxim ammunition, 75 mm shells, sighting equipment, and gun-carriage components became major supplies for the Hubei, Shanghai, and Nanjing forces. Different units nevertheless drew on separate batches, and spare parts and carriage fittings did not always match. The Beijing-Hankou railway, the Shanghai-Nanjing line, and Yangtze shipping determined the speed at which heavy guns, ammunition boxes, and wounded could be moved. Supply lines were repeatedly interrupted by railway junctions, bridge repairs, and shortages of horses.
tactics: 起義初期最有效的戰法，是先奪取軍械庫、通訊與交通節點，再迫使既有部隊選邊，而不是立即強攻完整設防的城市。武昌起義者先取楚望臺軍械庫，革命軍在蛇山及漢口正面部署砲位，利用漢陽軍械形成步槍與重機槍火力；清廷北洋軍則依托鐵路補給站、塹壕與固定砲位，以北洋各師的整建分隊逐次投入。陽羅作戰中，革命軍先以河岸砲兵壓制北洋軍前線，再由步兵奪取通往漢口的陣地，但各團進攻時間不一致，使優勢火力未能始終集中。十一月進攻南京時，滬軍、浙軍與鄂軍先以砲火控制城牆及紫金山附近陣地，再由步兵向缺口突入；守軍在連續失守砲台和外圍陣地後崩解。整體而言，革命軍的地方性強、指揮分散、彈藥補充不均，北洋軍的射擊與駐防較整齊，卻受制於長距離交通、地方反叛和清廷政治信用的崩潰。最終停戰主要靠軍隊改換效忠與政治協議，而不是一方被完全消滅。
tacticsEn: The most effective method at the beginning of the uprising was to seize arsenals, communications, and transport nodes before attempting a direct assault on a fully defended city. The Wuchang insurgents first took the Chu Wang Tai armory, while the revolutionaries deployed artillery on Snake Hill and along the Hankou front, using the Hanyang weapons to combine rifle and heavy-machine-gun fire. Qing Beiyang troops relied on railway supply depots, trenches, and fixed gun positions, committing their organized divisions in successive formations. During the Yangluo fighting, the revolutionaries first used riverbank artillery to suppress the Beiyang front and then sent infantry to seize the routes into Hankou. The attacks by individual regiments were not synchronized, however, so their superior firepower was not always concentrated. In the assault on Nanjing in November, troops from Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Hubei used artillery to control the city wall and the positions around Purple Mountain before infantry rushed through the breaches. The defending force disintegrated after losing its outer positions and artillery emplacements in sequence. Overall, the revolutionary forces had strong local initiative but suffered from divided command and uneven ammunition supply. The Beiyang forces possessed steadier fire discipline and a more coherent garrison system, yet their position was constrained by long supply routes, provincial revolts, and the collapse of the Qing government's political credibility. The eventual armistice depended chiefly on troops changing allegiance and on political agreements rather than on the complete destruction of one side.
data: 一九一一年三月二十九日，黃興在廣州率領的起義受挫，此後革命組織把重心移向駐防新軍。十月十日夜，武昌工程營等單位的起義者先取楚望臺軍械庫，再控制總督署與城內要點；十月十一日，革命軍奪得漢陽兵工廠，總督瑞澂撤離武昌。清廷把馮國璋、段祺瑞所部北洋軍調往鄂北，援軍沿京漢鐵路南下，十月十八日至十一月一日在漢口以南的陽羅一線交鋒，革命軍取得漢口；十一月初黃興抵達漢口整頓軍令，至十一月二十七日漢陽失守，革命軍由此聯通武昌、漢口與漢陽三鎮。與此同時，十月二十二日長沙、二十九日太原、三十日昆明相繼易幟；十一月三日上海革命軍取得江南製造局，五日杭州易幟，八日徐達等部攻下南京，九日廣東宣布脫離清廷，十一月二十七日四川宣布獨立。十一月下旬起，湖北、上海及其他省份的革命軍在南京設立中央軍事機構並籌劃北伐；十二月二十九日各省代表在南京推選孫中山為臨時大總統，一九一二年一月一日中華民國臨時政府在南京成立，一月二十八日臨時參議院成立。此後北洋軍各部在河南、河北與山西一帶維持對清廷的名義效忠，革命軍則缺乏統一北線指揮，彈藥和後勤補給又受京漢、津浦鐵路與地方軍隊動向牽制；一月底至二月初，唐紹儀等在上海與袁世凱方面代表談判，戰局遂由正面會戰轉為對軍隊效忠、政治職權和行政資源的交涉。
dataEn: On March 29, 1911, the uprising led by Huang Xing in Guangzhou was defeated, after which the revolutionary organizations shifted their focus toward the provincial New Armies. On the night of October 10, insurgents from the Hubei engineering battalion and other units first seized the Chu Wang Tai armory and then took control of the viceregal offices and key positions in the city. On October 11, the revolutionaries captured the Hanyang Arsenal, and Governor-General Ruicheng withdrew from Wuchang. The Qing court sent the Beiyang troops of Feng Guozhang and Duan Qirui toward northern Hubei, where the reinforcements moved south along the Beijing-Hankou railway. From October 18 to November 1 they fought along the Yangluo line south of Hankou, and the revolutionaries took Hankou. Huang Xing arrived at Hankou in early November to reorganize the command. When Hanyang fell on November 27, the revolutionaries connected Wuchang, Hankou, and Hanyang into a continuous position. At the same time, Changsha changed hands on October 22, Taiyuan on October 29, and Kunming on October 30. On November 3, the Shanghai revolutionaries captured the Jiangnan Arsenal; Hangzhou fell on the fifth; Xu Da and his troops took Nanjing on the eighth; Guangdong declared separation from the Qing on the ninth; and Sichuan declared independence on November 27. From late November, the Hubei, Shanghai, and other provincial revolutionary forces established central military institutions in Nanjing and planned the Northern Expeditions. On December 29, provincial representatives in Nanjing selected Sun Yat-sen as provisional president. The Provisional Government of the Republic of China was established in Nanjing on January 1, 1912, and the Provisional Senate was formed on January 28. Beiyang formations in Henan, Hebei, and Shanxi then maintained nominal loyalty to the Qing court, while the revolutionaries lacked a unified command on the northern front and suffered from ammunition and logistical constraints involving the Beijing-Hankou and Tianjin-Pukou railways and shifting provincial forces. From late January to early February, Tang Shaoyi and others negotiated in Shanghai with representatives of Yuan Shikai. The fighting consequently shifted from direct battles to an agreement over military allegiance, political authority, and administrative resources.
cause: 促成戰爭爆發的條件，來自清末軍政制度與革命組織長期形成的交會。晚清新政建立的新軍採用近代步槍、機槍、砲兵與較完整的軍令制度，湖北第八鎮等駐軍集中於省會，使少數經過協調的連營能迅速奪取軍械庫和控制城防。清廷為增加中央收入而推行川漢鐵路國有，與地方督撫、官僚及新軍的權力利益發生衝突；部分湖北新軍被調往四川，使武昌駐軍與後方之間出現失衡。湖北革命組織與同盟會成員在新軍、學校及省級機關中建立聯絡，形成策應起義的網絡。廣州起義失敗後，清廷加強偵緝與鎮壓，革命者便把行動集中到北方新軍可能響應的武昌。近代鐵路、電報與武器又使奪取兵工廠、車站和江防節點能迅速改變全省權力，而不必先控制全部領土。
causeEn: The conditions that produced the war arose from the convergence of late-Qing military and political institutions with long-term revolutionary organization. New Armies established during the late Qing New Policies adopted modern rifles, machine guns, artillery, and a more comprehensive command system. Provincial formations such as the Hubei Eighth Division were concentrated in provincial capitals, allowing a small number of coordinated companies to seize arsenals and city defenses rapidly. The Qing court's drive to increase central revenue through the nationalization of the Sichuan-Hankou railway conflicted with the authority and interests of provincial governors, officials, and New Army officers. Portions of the Hubei New Army were transferred to Sichuan, creating an imbalance between the garrison at Wuchang and its rear areas. Revolutionary organizations in Hubei and members of the Tongmenghui established contacts within New Army units, schools, and provincial offices, forming a network for coordinated uprisings. After the Guangzhou uprising failed, the Qing court intensified surveillance and repression, causing revolutionary leaders to concentrate their preparations at Wuchang, where northern New Army units might respond. Modern railways, telegraphs, and weapons also meant that taking an arsenal, railway station, or river-defense node could immediately transfer power across an entire province without first securing all its territory.
impact: 辛亥革命最深遠的制度結果，是清帝國與皇帝制度終止，中央權威改由臨時政府承擔，但原有軍隊並未因此組成統一的國家軍隊。各省軍政府掌握地方稅收、徵兵、軍械和任命權，革命軍與清軍的部隊都在改制後轉化為新的政治軍事集團；北洋軍尤其保有完整指揮系統與裝備，使袁世凱得以在清廷覆亡後迅速成為中央人物。南京政府遷往北京後，臨時約法、總統權限與北洋軍實際武力之間形成持續矛盾，開啟了以軍事實力決定政局的長期局面。技術與武器方面，漢陽、江南等兵工廠的存量和各省軍械在短時間內重新分配，鐵路沿線的戰略價值更為突出。外交方面，列強由承認清廷轉而承認民國政府，辛亥革命因此改變了中國對外交涉的政府形式。現存各役戰報分散，清廷、革命軍與各省檔案的統計標準不一，傷亡總數無法可靠相加；有明確記載者包括張人駿、張彪與陳其美等人的死亡，任何精確總數都不宜在缺乏原始核對時虛構。
impactEn: The deepest institutional result of the Xinhai Revolution was the end of the Qing Empire and the imperial system, with central authority passing to a provisional government, but the existing military forces did not thereby become a unified national army. The provincial military governments retained control over local taxation, recruitment, weapons, and appointments, while both revolutionary and Qing formations were converted into new political-military groups after the regime change. The Beiyang forces in particular preserved an integrated command system and substantial equipment, allowing Yuan Shikai to emerge rapidly as the central political figure after the Qing collapse. When the provisional government moved from Nanjing to Beijing, a lasting conflict developed among the Provisional Constitution, the formal powers of the president, and the actual military strength of the Beiyang armies. This opened a prolonged period in which political authority was decided by armed force. In terms of technology and materiel, the stocks of the Hanyang and Jiangnan arsenals and provincial weapons were redistributed within a short period, further increasing the strategic importance of the railways. Diplomatically, the powers shifted from recognizing the Qing court to recognizing the republican government, and the revolution consequently changed the form of government under which China conducted foreign relations. The surviving battle reports are dispersed, and Qing, revolutionary, and provincial records use different counting standards, so a reliable aggregate casualty total cannot be produced. The deaths of figures including Zhang Renjun, Zhang Biao, and Chen Qimei are specifically documented, but an exact total should not be invented without checking the original records.
result: 一月中旬，北洋將領要求由袁世凱主持大局，孫中山隨後表示，只要袁世凱赴北京、接受共和並尊重臨時約法，總統職位可以交付。1912年2月12日，清廷頒布退位詔，溥儀不再具有皇帝身分；2月15日孫中山解除臨時大總統職務並完成交接；3月10日袁世凱在北京就任中華民國臨時大總統，3月11日公布《中華民國臨時約法》。因此，戰爭的直接政治結果是清帝國終止、共和政府取得中央政權，而不是北洋軍被全殲或各省軍隊被統一編組。軍事上的未結項目仍然存在：各省仍有相對獨立的槍砲、指揮與財政系統，革命軍北伐未能形成常設統一軍，臨時約法與總統實權之間也很快出現衝突。結果既是帝制崩解，也是軍權地方化與總統集權化的起點。
resultEn: In the middle of January, the Beiyang commanders demanded that Yuan Shikai take charge of the situation. Sun Yat-sen then indicated that the presidency could be transferred provided Yuan went to Beijing, accepted the republican system, and respected the Provisional Constitution. On February 12, 1912, the Qing court issued the abdication edict, and Puyi ceased to hold the status of emperor. On February 15, Sun Yat-sen resigned as provisional president and completed the transfer. Yuan Shikai was inaugurated as Provisional President of the Republic of China in Beijing on March 10, and the Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China was promulgated on March 11. The direct political result of the war was therefore the termination of the Qing Empire and the transfer of central authority to a republican government, not the annihilation of the Beiyang army or the unified organization of all provincial forces. Major military questions remained unresolved. Each province still controlled relatively separate weapons, commands, and finances; the revolutionary Northern Expeditions never developed into a permanent unified army; and conflict quickly arose between the Provisional Constitution and the actual power of the president. The outcome was both the collapse of imperial rule and the beginning of localized military power and presidential centralization.
